newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-TIGER FERVOUR SWEEPS AUSTRALIA BEFORE OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER FERVOUR SWEEPS AUSTRALIA BEFORE OPEN.

text.p: The fervour surrounding golfer Tiger Woods has spread to Australia with soaring ticket sales for the American's first professional appearance overseas, tournament officials said on Tuesday.

Woods, 20, who has already won twice on the U.S. PGA Tour since leaving the amateur ranks two months ago, will appear alongside world number one and local favourite Greg Norman at next month's Australian Open in Sydney.
The Australian Golf Union (AGU) has attributed a 40 percent increase in ticket sales compared with last year to Woods's presence and the prospect of a showdown with Norman.
Prime corporate hospitality facilities were sold in record time for the A$1.0 million (US$790,000) tournament at The Australian course between November 21 and 24, AGU director Colin Phillips said.

"Ticket sales...are up by about 40 percent on what they were at the same time for the Open in Melbourne last year," he told Reuters. "We are expecting a crowd of about 25,000 each day, compared with about 18,000 or so in 1995."
"It's the first time corporate facilities around the 18th green have all been sold a month before the tournament."

Woods, who used his awesome length off the tee to post five consecutive top-five finishes in a stunning start to his professional career, was reportedly paid A$230,000 in appearance money to play in Australia.
Phillips said Woods received a lower fee but declined to give details.
Norman is chasing his fifth national Open title on one of his regular visits to his native Australia.
"Having these two players together in Australia has made it enormously interesting for people," Phillips said.
